facts.statement: Aeolosaurus lived during the Late Cretaceous period.
facts.quote: fossil_range: Late Cretaceous

facts.statement: The type species Aeolosaurus rionegrinus was discovered in the Angostura Colorada Formation in Argentina, dating from 83 to 74 million years ago.
facts.quote: It was discovered in the Angostura Colorada Formation in Argentina, which dates from the Campanian stage of the Late Cretaceous, about 83 to 74 million years ago.

facts.statement: The holotype of Aeolosaurus rionegrinus includes seven tail vertebrae and parts of the forelimbs and right hindlimb.
facts.quote: The holotype of Aeolosaurus rionegrinus consists of a series of seven tail vertebrae, as well as parts of both forelimbs and the right hindlimb.

facts.statement: No skull remains are known for Aeolosaurus.
facts.quote: However, like most titanosaurs, no remains of the skull are known.

facts.statement: The genus and type species Aeolosaurus rionegrinus were named and described by Jaime Powell in 1987.
facts.quote: Both genus and species were named and described by Argentine paleontologist Jaime Powell in 1987.

facts.statement: The name Aeolosaurus honors the Greek mythological figure Aeolus due to the frequent winds in Patagonia where fossils were found.
facts.quote: This dinosaur is named after the Greek mythological figure Aeolus, Keeper of the Winds in Homer's Odyssey, because of the frequent winds that blow across Patagonia, where the remains were found.

facts.statement: The specific name rionegrinus refers to the Rio Negro Province in Argentina.
facts.quote: The specific name (A. rionegrinus), refers to its location, in the Rio Negro Province of Argentina.

facts.statement: Aeolosaurus fossils are found across South America during the Late Cretaceous.
facts.quote: Aeolosaurus is a widespread genus of titanosaur known from the Late Cretaceous of South America.

facts.statement: Aeolosaurus fossils have been collected from formations in Argentina and Brazil.
facts.quote: Fossils have been collected from the Allen, Angostura Colorada, Lago Colhué Huapí, and Los Alamitos Formations of Argentina and the Serra da Galga Formation of Brazil.

facts.statement: All known Aeolosaurus fossils date to the Campanian and Maastrichtian ages of the Cretaceous.
facts.quote: All Aeolosaurus fossils are from the Campanian and Maastrichtian ages of the Cretaceous period.

facts.statement: Gregory S. Paul estimated Aeolosaurus rionegrinus was about 14 meters long and weighed 6 tonnes.
facts.quote: A. rionegrinus was roughly 14 meters (46 ft) long and 6 tonnes (6.6 short tons) in weight according to Gregory S. Paul.

facts.statement: Molina-Pérez and Larramendi estimated Aeolosaurus rionegrinus could reach 18.1 meters in length and 14.7 tonnes in weight.
facts.quote: In 2020 Molina-Pérez and Larramendi gave a larger estimation of 18.1 meters (60 ft) and 14.7 tonnes (16.2 short tons).

facts.statement: Aeolosaurus rionegrinus had limb bones as robust as those of Saltasaurus.
facts.quote: A. rionegrinus was heavily built for a titanosaur, with limb bones similar in robustness to those of Saltasaurus.

facts.statement: Aeolosaurus possesses very distinctive tail vertebrae.
facts.quote: Aeolosaurs, Aeolosaurus in particular, have very distinctive caudal vertebrae.

facts.statement: The tail of Aeolosaurus was strongly curved downward, a trait likely shared with other Aeolosaurini.
facts.quote: The tail of Aeolosaurus was apparently curved strongly downward, a trait likely shared with other members of Aeolosaurini.

facts.statement: Aeolosaurus bore osteoderms, similar to many lithostrotian titanosaurs.
facts.quote: Aeolosaurus, like many lithostrotian titanosaurs, bore osteoderms.

facts.statement: In 2004, Aeolosaurus and Gondwanatitan were grouped together in the clade Aeolosaurini.
facts.quote: In 2004, Aeolosaurus and Gondwanatitan were recognized as forming a new group of titanosaurs, which was named Aeolosaurini.

facts.statement: A second species, Aeolosaurus colhuehuapensis, was named in 2007 from Patagonia.
facts.quote: In 2007, a second species, A. colhuehuapensis was named, also from Patagonia.

facts.statement: A third species, Aeolosaurus maximus, was named in 2011.
facts.quote: A third species, A. maximus, was named in 2011.

facts.statement: Aeolosaurus maximus was transferred to the genus Arrudatitan in 2021.
facts.quote: A. maximus was moved to the genus Arrudatitan in 2021.

facts.statement: There are currently two valid named species of Aeolosaurus, plus several unnamed specimens.
facts.quote: There are currently two named valid species of Aeolosaurus, as well as several specimens that have been referred to the genus but not given a species.

facts.statement: Scientists have not formally named two possible new Aeolosaurus species due to the genus being poorly known.
facts.quote: However, since the genus Aeolosaurus is not well known, the authors chose not to formally name either of these possible new species.

facts.statement: Aeolosaurus shared its Late Cretaceous environment with hadrosaurs.
facts.quote: Aeolosaurus lived during the Campanian and Maastrichtian ages of the Late Cretaceous and shared its environment with hadrosaurs.

facts.statement: An unnamed Aeolosaurus species from the Allen Formation lived alongside five other titanosaur species, hadrosaurs, and ankylosaurs.
facts.quote: The unnamed Allen Formation species of Aeolosaurus inhabited an environment that it shared with five other species of titanosaur, including Rocasaurus muniozi, as well as hadrosaurs and ankylosaurs.

facts.statement: Aeolosaurus lived during the late Cretaceous Campanian stage, approximately 74 to 70 million years ago, in what is now South America.
facts.quote: que vivieron a finales del período Cretácico, en el Campaniense, hace aproximadamente 74 a 70 millones de años, en lo que hoy es Sudamérica.

facts.statement: The genus Aeolosaurus was described by paleontologist Jaime Powell in 1987, who named the type species Aeolosaurus rionegrinus.
facts.quote: El género fue descrito por el paleontólogo Jaime Powell en 1987, quien describió la especie tipo A. rionegrinus.

facts.statement: A second species, Aeolosaurus colhuehuapensis, was described by Casal et al. in 2007.
facts.quote: Una segunda especie, Aeolosaurus colhuehuapensis, fue descrita por Casal et al. en 2007.

facts.statement: Aeolosaurus was a large, long-necked, quadrupedal herbivore measuring around 14 meters in length.
facts.quote: Aeolosaurus era un herbívoro de cuello largo, grande, cuadrúpedo, medían alrededor de los 14 metros de longitud.

facts.statement: The type species A. rionegrinus had a robust build with limb bones similar in strength to Saltasaurus, whereas A. maximus appears to have been more slender.
facts.quote: La especie tipo, A. rionegrinus tenía una constitución fuerte para un titanosaurio, con huesos de las extremidades similares en robustez a los de Saltasaurus, mientras que A. maximus parece haber sido más delgado.

facts.statement: Aeolosaurus is diagnosed by distinctive tail vertebrae featuring downward-curving prezygapophyses in anterior vertebrae and chevrons with concave posterodorsal surfaces containing double anterior articular facets.
facts.quote: Aeolosaurus , en particular, tiene vértebras caudales muy distintivas, se diagnostica por la presencia compartida de prezigapófisis curvas hacia abajo en su vértebras caudales anteriores y los cheurones de las partes centrales de la cola con superficies posterodorsales cóncavas que contienen facetas dobles articular anterior.

facts.statement: The osteoderms of Aeolosaurus were unusual, with most resembling those of Mendozasaurus.
facts.quote: sus osteodermos eran inusuales y la mayoría se parecen mucho a las de Mendozasaurus.

facts.statement: Like in all titanosaur osteoderms, Aeolosaurus osteoderms were likely arranged in one or two rows along the body flanks.
facts.quote: Al igual que en todos los osteodermos de titanosaurios, los suyos probablemente estaban dispuestos en una o dos hileras a lo largo de los flancos del cuerpo.

facts.statement: The holotype MJG-R 1 of Aeolosaurus rionegrinus consists of a series of seven vertebrae, with most of both hind limbs and the right forelimb.
facts.quote: El holotipo, MJG-R 1, de Aeolosaurus rionegrinus consiste en una serie de siete vértebras, con buena parte de ambos miembros posteriores y de la pata delantera derecha.

facts.statement: The holotype was found in the Angostura Colorada Formation in Argentina, dated to the Campanian of the Late Cretaceous, approximately 83 to 74 million years ago.
facts.quote: Fue descubierto en la Formación Angostura Colorada en Argentina, datada en el Campaniano durante el Cretácico superior hace alrededor de 83 a 74 millones de años.

facts.statement: The second species A. colhuehuapensis was found in the Bajo Barreal Formation between the Campanian and Maastrichtian, on the shores of Lake Colhué Huapi in Chubut Province, based on a series of twenty-one tail vertebrae.
facts.quote: La segunda especie A. colhuehuapensis fue encontrado en la Formación Bajo Barreal, entre el Campaniano y el Maastrichtiense, en la riveras del Lago Colhué Huapi, en la Provincia del Chubut, basándose en una serie de veintiún vértebras caudales.

facts.statement: The third species, A. maximus, is the largest and is known from an incomplete skeleton including cervical, dorsal, and tail vertebrae, ribs, and appendicular elements found in the Adamantina Formation, Brazil.
facts.quote: La tercera especie, A. maximus, es la más grande, y es conocida a partir de un esqueleto incompleto incluyendo vértebras cervicales, dorsales y caudales, costillas, y los elementos apendiculares hallado en la Formación Adamantina, Brasil.

facts.statement: Associated osteoderms provide evidence that this dinosaur was armored.
facts.quote: Estos huesos también fueron asociados a dos osteodermos, proporcionando evidencia que este dinosaurio era acorazado.

facts.statement: This specimen is from the Allen Formation of Río Negro, dating to approximately 70 to 68 million years ago in the middle Maastrichtian.
facts.quote: Este espécimen es de la Formación Allen de río Negro, datando hace aproximadamente de 70 a 68 millones de años a mediados del Maastrichtiense.

facts.statement: Additional material from the same quarry, described in 2013, shows the quarry contained the remains of at least three Aeolosaurus individuals.
facts.quote: El material adicional de la misma cantera, descrito en 2013, muestra que la cantera contenía los restos de al menos tres individuos de Aeolosaurus.

facts.statement: Because the genus Aeolosaurus is not well known, authors chose not to formally name these potential new species.
facts.quote: Sin embargo, puesto que el género Aeolosaurus no es bien conocido, los autores eligieron no nombrar formalmente tampoco de estas nuevas especies posibles.

facts.statement: Gondwanatitan faustoi, the closest known relative, has been proposed to represent an additional Aeolosaurus species, but Gondwanatitan is normally considered a distinct genus.
facts.quote: Gondwanatitan faustoi, el pariente más cercano conocido del género, se ha propuesto para representar una especie adicional de Aeolosaurus, como A. faustoi. Sin embargo, Gondwanatitan se considera normalmente un género distinto.

facts.statement: In 2004, Franco-Costa et al. established the clade Aeolosaurini to include Aeolosaurus rionegrinus and Gondwanatitan faustoi.
facts.quote: en 2004 Franco-Costa et al. erigió el clado Aeolosaurini como el clado más inclusivo que contiene a Aeolosaurus rionegrinus y Gondwanatitan faustoi

facts.statement: In 2016, Franca et al. placed Aeolosaurus and its relatives in the family Aeolosauridae as the sister taxon to Saltasauridae within the superfamily Saltasauroidea.
facts.quote: En 2016 Franca et al., colocan a Aeolosaurus y todos sus relativos en la familia Aeolosauridae como taxón hermano de Saltasauridae dentro de la superfamilia Saltasauroidea

facts.statement: Gondwanatitan and Aeolosaurus both exhibit dorsal neural spines on caudal vertebrae pointing backward, a feature not seen in other known titanosaurs.
facts.quote: Gondwanatitan y Aeolosaurus ambos exhiben espinas neurales dorsales de las vértebras caudales hacia atrás, una característica no vista en otros titanosaurianos conocidos

facts.statement: Aeolosaurus lived from the Campanian to the Maastrichtian, between 83.6 and 66 million years ago.
facts.quote: Time range: Campanian to Maastrichtian (83.6 to 66 million years ago)

facts.statement: Aeolosaurus is a widespread genus of titanosaurs known from the late Cretaceous of South America.
facts.quote: Aeolosaurus es un género muy extendido de titanosaurios conocido de finales el cretácico de América del Sur

facts.statement: All Aeolosaurus fossils come from Campanian and Maastrichtian rocks, and these animals lived alongside hadrosaurs.
facts.quote: Todos los fósiles de Aeolosaurus provienen de rocas de las edades Campaniense y Maastrichtiense del período Cretácico los Aeolosaurios vivieron en el campaniano y maastrichtiano compartiendo el espacio con hadrosáuridos

facts.statement: Fossils have been collected from the Allen, Angostura Colorada, Bajo Barreal, and Los Alamitos Formations in Argentina, and the Adamantina and Marília Formations in Brazil.
facts.quote: Los fósiles se han recogido de Formación Allen, Formación Angostura Colorada, Formación Bajo Barreal, y Formación Los Alamitos de Argentina y de la Formación Adamantina y Formación Marília de Brasil

facts.statement: The unnamed Allen Formation species shared its environment with five other titanosaur species, including Rocasaurus muniozi, as well as hadrosaurs and ankylosaurs.
facts.quote: la especie de la Formación Allen aún sin nombrar compartió su ambiente con 5 especies de titanosaurios, incluyendo Rocasaurus muniozi así como hadrosáuridos y anquilosauridos

facts.statement: Titanosaurian relationships are obscure at best, but Aeolosaurus has been tentatively linked to other genera like Rinconsaurus and Adamantisaurus based on tail vertebra characteristics.
facts.quote: Las relaciones entre los muchos titanosaurianos son oscuras en el mejor de los casos, pero Aeolosaurus se ha ligado tentativamente a algunos otros géneros, basados en las características de las vértebras de la cola, incluyendo Rinconsaurus y Adamantisaurus
